newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet to add three cities with $49 fare.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet to add three cities with $49 fare.

text.p: ValuJet Inc. said Monday it will add flights to Dallas/Fort Worth, West Palm Beach, Fla., and Fort Myers, Fla., on Dec. 19 with a fare of $49.

In an interview with NBC affiliate WXIA-TV, Valujet President Lewis Jordan said the discount airline's expansion plans remain on tract despite last week's National Transportation Safety Board hearings into the May 11 crash of ValuJet flight 592.
The airline resumed operations in October after being grounded for three months by Federal authorities as a result of a probe into the crash in the Florida Everglades that killed 110 people.

The report also said that ValuJet planned to ask the Federal Aviation Administration for permission to put five more planes into service, bringing overall flight operations to 20 aircraft with 138 daily departures from Atlanta.
Also on Monday, ValuJet was set to begin offering special fares of $39, $49, $59 and $69 to all its destinations for travel between Dec. 3 through Dec. 18.
Asked by an interviewer if ValuJet's expansion plans were "on track," Jordan responded: "Yes, they are. As you know, they're subject to FAA approval, but we believe that we will be going forward."

Jordan said a ValuJet flight was forced to return to Orlando on Saturday after a passenger reported smelling an electrical odour but that it did not represent an emergency and was rather a precaution.
"We found that we had an electrical circuit that had popped a circuit breaker. It had a little electrical smell. We removed those components for analysis to see exactly what it was," Jordan said.
"But it certainly was not an emergency. It was a precautionary step. But because it's ValuJet, we got a lot of attention," he said.
The incident followed a week of NTSB hearings in which an FAA inspector complained that his efforts had been overwhelmed by the discount carrier's rapid growth in the run-up to the May 11 crash.

Jordan said Monday that the hearings could result in industry-wide changes but added that he believes the proceedings "missed the point" by focusing on ValuJet in examining issues that have affected big carriers for years.
"It's certain there will be changes made in the industry -- changes that will affect our company," he said.
